title: Linux owned-server drain: /proc scan ignores the drain deadline, and descriptor exhaustion abandons live children
outcome: (1) The 30 s drain deadline is checked only after children_of returns, so on a very large process table a scan that crosses the deadline still reads every remaining /proc stat before the stopped server is killed, delaying other queued cleanups on the one worker. (2) Each signalled child keeps its pidfd through the round; under low descriptor headroom later pidfd_open calls get EMFILE and those pids are permanently abandoned, so live children can be orphaned when the server is killed.
acceptance: The /proc enumeration honours the drain deadline and returns a partial result, so the root kill is reached when the budget expires.
EMFILE on pidfd_open is retried within the deadline after the round's pins are dropped, instead of abandoning the pid; a behaviour test with a lowered descriptor limit shows all children ended.
